 Brazoria County District Court
 Cause No. 2026-CV-0013
 Kathleen Garcia, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Oral Deposition of Kathleen Garcia
Date:
June 3, 2026
Location:
Offices of Gardner & Morris Law Group
Examining attorney:
Stephanie Williams, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defending attorney:
Sergio Acosta, Gardner & Morris Law Group
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not put my full name on the transcript today, if that's all right. You can use the case caption.
Q: That's fine for now. Where were you on the day of the collision?
A: I was driving home from work on a weekday evening. I was stopped at a red light on the main road in Baytown, waiting to
turn.
Q: Tell me what happened next.
A: I was sitting still with my foot on the brake when I felt a hard jolt from behind. My head snapped forward and back, and my
car got pushed into the intersection. The other driver's front bumper was crushed into my rear.
Q: Did you have your hands on the wheel at the time?
A: Yes, both hands. I remember my right hand was on the wheel and my left hand was on the gear shift. When the impact hit, my
right arm was thrown against the door frame.
Q: Did you get out of the vehicle?
A: I got out after a few minutes. My wrist was already swelling and hurting badly, and I could barely grip anything.
Q: What treatment did you receive for your wrist?
A: I went to the emergency room that night. They took X-rays and told me the wrist was broken. I was put in a splint and given
instructions to see an orthopedic doctor. A few days later I had a follow-up appointment, and the doctor said I would need a cast
for several weeks.
Q: Have you had any further treatment since then?
A: Yes. I went to physical therapy twice a week for a while. The therapist had me doing exercises to rebuild grip strength and
range of motion. Some days were better than others.
Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: It's made ordinary things hard. Cooking, opening jars, and buttoinng my shirt were difficult for a long time. I'm right-handed,
so I had to learn to do almost everything with my left hand. I also had to stop my weekend yard work and my volunteer shifts for
a while.
Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms today?
A: Yes, I still notice stiffness in the mornings, and when the weather turns cold, the wrist aches. I can lift things, but I avoid
heavy loads because I worry about pushing too hard.
Q: Have you returned to your regular work duties?
A: I went back on modified duty first, then eventually to full duty. I'm working now, but I was out for a period and my hours were
reduced during recovery.
</page>
